offence_severity: Life imprisonment and a fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default, to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months
physical_harm: The deceased had bruises on her body and marks of violence, and her nose was bleeding with blood clots on her cheeks
number_of_offences: Five offences were charged, but only one was finally upheld against the appellant
key_evidence_accepted: Statement of witnesses provided a complete chain as to how the deceased was last seen with the appellant whereafter she died and her body was cremated in the village despite protest by her parents.
witness_credibility: The statements of witnesses established the facts which formed the very basis of the case of the prosecution.
post_offence_conduct: The accused immediately returned to Belgaum. The dead body of the deceased was cremated despite protest by her parents.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 7th October, 1993; Trial judgment: 18th January, 2000; High Court decision: 19th December, 2003; Supreme Court decision: May 8, 2012
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Seeraj Bagga (A.C.); Counsel for the State: V.N. Raghupathy, Azeen A. Kalebudde
investigation_status: FIR filed subsequently; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquitted all accused except appellant; High Court: Upheld trial court's decision; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the victim-deceased was last seen with the appellant whereafter she died, and the statements of witnesses established the facts forming the basis of the case. The prosecution also emphasized that the accused failed to provide any explanation for the deceased's death despite being last seen with her.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the case was based on circumstantial evidence and that the prosecution failed to establish a complete chain of events pointing to the appellant's guilt. They also contended that the appellant had participated in taking the deceased to the hospital and attended her funeral, absolving him of liability.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that when evidence is legally admissible and has been appreciated by the courts in its correct perspective, the Court would be very reluctant to interfere with the concurrent findings of the courts below merely because another view is possible.
precedent_relied_upon: Kali Ram v. State of H.P. (1973) 2 SCC 808; Amarsingh Munnasingh Suryawanshi v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 15 SCC 455; Birendar Poddar v. State of Bihar (2011) 6 SCC 350; Sucha Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab (2003) 7 SCC 64S; Asraf Ali v. State of Assam (2008) 16 SCC 328; Manu Sao v. State of Bihar (2010) 12 SCC 310; Mousam Singha Roy & Ors. v. State of WB. (2003) 12 SCC 377
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution established the complete chain of events pointing to the guilt of the appellant, and the courts below found the evidence legally admissible and appreciated in consonance with the rules of prudence and law.
other_sentence_order: The Director General of Police/Commissioner of Police, Karnataka is directed to take disciplinary action against the police officers/officials at Belgaum and village Gokarna who failed to act appropriately in the case.
